source.title: On the importance of single directions for generalization
source.authors: Ari S. Morcos; D. G. Barrett; N. Rabinowitz; M. Botvinick

record.tranche_reason: Tests how training on corrupted labels relates to network reliance on single directions, using activation ablations and noise perturbations rather than the original study's generalization measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training networks on varying fractions of randomized labels and explicitly says training accuracy was approximately 1 for all networks tested. Its main reported results concern ablation and noise sensitivity; those are not rows for the claim versions unless they measure a named behavior. Figure 5's ablation curves are not training-fit measurements.
record.test_reason: The study directly repeats randomized-label training and reports approximately perfect training accuracy. Its main ablation analyses measure a different construct. Its dropout experiment also bears on V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record correctly summarizes the principal ablation result but omits a relevant qualification: the authors find that dropout discourages memorization, with slower convergence and worse solutions at higher dropout probabilities. They conclude that generalization is associated with reduced reliance on single directions, and that dropout does not regularize this reliance beyond its training dropout fraction.
record.recipe_differences: Trains networks on partially corrupted labels, then measures sensitivity to activation-space ablation and noise; this differs from directly cataloging train and test error under random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports that ablation curves are not always perfectly ordered by corruption fraction. Dropout probability also changes convergence time and solution quality in the dropout experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Corrupted-label networks are more sensitive to cumulative activation ablations and Gaussian activation noise than true-label networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Memorizing networks rely more strongly on individual activation directions.

record.problems: For the random-label fitting result, the text gives an aggregate approximate training-accuracy statement without per-model or per-fraction values, and does not report corresponding test error or a matched unchanged-hyperparameter comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows for the claim versions: the paper's cumulative ablation and random-noise perturbation outcomes measure reliance on single directions, not the training or test behavior specified by the other versions.

untested.parts: Chance-level test error is not reported. An unchanged-hyperparameter comparison is not established; corrupted-label ImageNet training explicitly omitted augmentation. ImageNet top-1 training fit is not reported.
No training-time ratio for random versus true labels or convergence-time trend across corruption fractions is reported. The dropout-dependent convergence observation does not establish either.
No fitting experiments with shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs. Gaussian activation perturbations are a different experiment.
Steady test-error degradation toward chance and retention of the remaining signal are not measured across corruption fractions.

Weight decay and generalization after removing explicit regularization are not tested. No augmentation-on versus augmentation-off random-label fitting result is reported; the augmentation statement is an argument explaining a design choice.
No comparison of when shared real-label patterns and noisy labels are learned.

missing.what: Dropout-dependent random-label fitting: MNIST MLPs required more epochs to converge and reached worse solutions at higher dropout probabilities. Record the qualitative final-fit result separately from ablation sensitivity; numerical final accuracies are unavailable in the supplied text.

The authors explicitly argue that augmentation would prevent memorization by increasing effective training-set size, and therefore omit it for corrupted-label ImageNet training. Record this as an argument and experimental condition, not an observed augmentation-control result.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its ablation endpoint at chance is performance after removing all directions, not evidence of chance-level test performance on random labels. The approximately perfect training-accuracy statement in Section 3.1 should not be extended to the separate dropout experiment.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report test error at chance for the random-label fits or establish that architecture and training hyperparameters remained unchanged relative to true-label training.
The paper mentions longer convergence for dropout networks, but does not test training time as a function of corrupted-label fraction or compare time against true-label training.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input fitting experiment.
Does not report test error across label-corruption fractions or establish steady degradation toward chance while training fit remains perfect.

Tests dropout's effect on reliance on single directions and reports convergence differences, but does not establish that weight decay, dropout, and augmentation fail to prevent random-label fitting or that removing them leaves true-label generalization intact.
Does not measure whether real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels.

rows.subject: 2-hidden layer MLP trained on MNIST; 11-layer convolutional network trained on CIFAR-10; 50-layer residual network trained on ImageNet
rows.size_stated: 2-hidden layer MLP; 11-layer convolutional network; 50-layer residual network
rows.operation_detail: Trained on datasets with differing fractions of randomized labels; training accuracy used to evaluate performance for corrupted-label models.
rows.locator: Section 3.1, paragraph beginning “To test whether memorization leads”
rows.note: Aggregate statement across the networks tested; no per-model or per-corruption-fraction accuracy is given.
rows.check: The aggregate training-fit statement is accurate but supports only the training-fit components of these versions. ImageNet accuracy is top-5, so it does not establish near-zero top-1 training error. Separate models and corruption fractions where possible. Appendix A.2 specifies that data augmentation was omitted for corrupted-label ImageNet training.
